key_insight: Picard–Chebyshev weakly nonlinear analysis predicts how streak–planar-wave interactions generate oblique and harmonic waves that can trigger streak breakdown.
engineering_relevance: Predicting finite-amplitude transition triggers could inform disturbance control and laminar-flow preservation in wall-bounded flows.
method: Formulate weakly nonlinear optimal perturbation analysis for compressible parallel flows.
Track non-modal amplification and nonlinear interactions across an expanding set of wavenumbers.
Use successive Picard–Chebyshev approximations to approach DNS in the weakly nonlinear regime.
evidence_signal: For subcritical plane Poiseuille flow at Mach 0.3 and Reynolds number 3000, the abstract reports high agreement with DNS and identifies an optimal planar-wave perturbation that triggers streak breakdown in full nonlinear simulation.
watch_item: Demonstrated accuracy is limited to the reported flow conditions; reliability beyond the weakly nonlinear regime remains to be established.
paper_title: Predicting trigger in streak breakdown via Picard-Chebyshev approach in plane-Poiseuille flow
